organization_or_origin: Paris engraving and sheet publication network

description.summary: An engraved Enlightenment-era survey style: cream paper, black/brown copperplate linework, dense place names, roads, rivers, forests, churches and settlements, sheet margins, measured framework, and approximate hachured relief. The map should feel scientific and royal-state systematic, not fanciful pirate parchment. Sacrebleu, but with triangulation.
description.design_principle: Express national survey precision through engraved restraint: monochrome or lightly hand-colored linework, dense named geography, hachured relief, road and settlement symbols, neat sheet structure, and formal cloud web mapping platformuche/marginalia.
description.historical_context: The Cassini Carte de France was a large national survey project, based on geodetic triangulation and published as adjoining engraved sheets. It represented an unprecedented systematic mapping of France's territory, settlements, roads, hydrography, and relief in the eighteenth century. copperplate engraving black ink impressions on cream/ivory paper hand coloring in selected surviving exemplars

General geographic orientation, feature lookup, and broad contextual reading. This brief is ranked 2 with a primary role based on its source classification and curated migration profile.
Elevation, landform, contours, hillshade, bathymetry, and relief as the principal subject. This brief is ranked 3 with a hybrid role based on its source classification and curated migration profile.
Settlements, boundaries, culture, population, political geography, and human networks. This brief is ranked 4 with a hybrid role based on its source classification and curated migration profile.

subjects: churches, abbeys, mills, castles, and other landmarks

behavior: Default should be black/sepia engraving on ivory paper.
Use color only as transparent hand-applied wash, never as modern flat thematic fill.
If roads are highlighted, use ochre or slightly heavier ink rather than bright modern colors.
Forests may use a pale green wash plus engraved tree/texture marks; water may use faint blue wash plus black river engraving.

typography.character: Engraved old-style serif and copperplate-like italic mix. Place labels should feel hand-engraved, with elegant variation in size, slope, spacing, and curvature. Avoid Victorian display fonts; Cassini is earlier and more scientific.
typography.fallback_strategy: Prefer metrically stable, licensable fonts with the language coverage required by the map; preserve hierarchy when substitution is necessary.
rules: Use many place labels; dense naming is part of the style.
Allow slight rotation and curvature to follow rivers, coasts, roads, or regional spread.
Prefer old-style serifs and italics; do not use modern sans-serif labels.
Use long-s characters only with extreme caution; legibility beats antiquarian showing-off.

linework: Fine engraved black/sepia linework with varied pressure, slight wobble, cross-hatching, and small symbolic marks. Use line density instead of color to differentiate features.

required: Express national survey precision through engraved restraint: monochrome or lightly hand-colored linework, dense named geography, hachured relief, road and settlement symbols, neat sheet structure, and formal cloud web mapping platformuche/marginalia.
preferred: Use ivory paper, sepia/black engraved lines, old-style serif typography, and hachured relief.
Use antique marginalia: cloud web mapping platformuche, scale, sheet number, neatline, and source note.
Do not use modern contours, hillshade gradients, or satellite imagery.
Do not turn it into a fantasy treasure map with burnt edges and skulls. Absolutely not; history has suffered enough.
Do not use bright thematic fills or default web map pins.
Generate hachures from terrain slope/aspect if possible, or use hand-drawn hachure textures clipped to relief zones.
For polygons, use hatching, stipple, or transparent wash instead of flat opaque fill.
Treat label density as a feature, but provide a web legibility mode at small screens.
Mobile: use a magnified viewport or forced landscape for detailed Cassini facsimile; otherwise offer cleaned label mode.
avoid: modern French national mapping topographic map
unsupported: Exact facsimile reproduction of a named source map, protected artwork, logo, seal, interface, or trade dress.
Provider-specific behavior that has not been verified against a pinned source and style contract.

accessibility.color_independence: Authentic low-contrast antique palettes can be difficult on screens. Provide an optional 'legible facsimile' mode with slightly darker ink and cleaner halos/paper contrast while preserving the engraved aesthetic.
accessibility.contrast: Preserve readable contrast for labels, lines, and critical symbols at intended zoom levels.
accessibility.minimum_text_size: Adapt historical or print typography to a practical screen-reading threshold.
additional: Test the compiled style in grayscale and under common color-vision simulations.
